gold_statement: The system shall keep application time within five minutes of the official NIST time source.
statement: The system shall ensure that the application time stays within five minutes of the NIST time source.

gold_statement: The system shall digitally sign the required prescription information and archive the digitally signed record.
statement: The system shall archive the digitally signed record of the prescription.

gold_statement: The system shall protect audit records from modification and deletion.
statement: The system shall protect the stored audit records from unauthorized deletion and modifications.

gold_statement: The system shall record in each audit record the date and time, the event type, the identity of the person acting and the outcome.
statement: The system shall record within each audit record the date and time of the event, the type of event, the identity of the person taking the action, and the outcome (success or failure).

gold_statement: The system shall include an indication that the prescribing practitioner signed the prescription in every transmitted controlled-substance prescription.
statement: The system shall indicate that the prescribing practitioner has signed every controlled prescription.

gold_statement: The system shall require a second designated individual who is a DEA registrant to approve each signing-access change using two-factor authentication.
statement: Granting or revoking signing access shall be entered by one designated person and approved by a second designated person who is a DEA registrant using two-factor authentication.

gold_statement: The system shall store the application's private signing key encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.
statement: The system shall retain the private signing key encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.

gold_statement: The system shall transmit a signed controlled-substance prescription to the pharmacy without converting it to facsimile or any other form.
statement: The system shall transmit signed controlled substances prescriptions to the pharmacy.

gold_statement: The credentialing process shall verify government photographic ID, state licence and DEA registration before a signing credential is issued.
statement: The system shall verify government photo ID, state license, and DEA registration before a practitioner's credential is issued.

gold_statement: The system shall analyse the audit trail every calendar day and generate an incident report of auditable events.
statement: The system shall generate an incident report that identifies each auditable event at least once every calendar day.

gold_statement: The system shall require two-factor authentication using two of a knowledge factor, a biometric and a hard token to sign a controlled-substance prescription.
statement: The system shall require two-factor authentication at the signing function for controlled substances prescriptions.

gold_statement: The system shall require the practitioner to select the DEA registration number to place on the prescription when the practitioner holds more than one.
statement: The system shall include the patient's DEA registration information on the prescription and ask which DEA registration to use when the patient has more than one, as stated in S-PRES-30.

gold_statement: The system shall retain controlled-substance records electronically for two years in a readily retrievable form.
statement: The system shall maintain records related to controlled substance prescriptions for two years.

gold_statement: The system shall limit a single signing action to controlled-substance prescriptions for one patient.
statement: The system shall ensure that each signing action covers prescriptions for a single patient only.

gold_statement: The application shall pass a third-party EPCS audit before it is used for controlled-substance prescriptions.
statement: NFR-EPCS-048: The system shall undergo a third-party EPCS audit before it can be used for controlled substances.

gold_statement: The system shall time- and date-stamp each controlled-substance prescription when it is signed.
statement: The system shall time and date stamp the prescription within 20 seconds when the signing function is used.

gold_statement: The system shall give each practitioner a log of the previous month's controlled-substance prescriptions within seven days of month end, sortable by patient, drug and date of issuance.
statement: The system shall generate monthly prescription logs for controlled substances.

gold_statement: The system shall require the practitioner to indicate that each controlled-substance prescription is ready for signing before the signing prompt is shown.
statement: The system shall require the prescriber to authenticate using a hard token and at least one additional factor for signing controlled substance prescriptions.

gold_statement: The system shall cancel a controlled-substance prescription if any required information is altered after it has been signed.
statement: The system shall not transmit a controlled prescription unless the signing function has been used.

gold_statement: The system shall treat any alteration of prescription content during transmission as invalidating the prescription.
statement: The system shall ensure that the electronic prescription data is not altered during transmission between the practitioner and pharmacy.

gold_statement: The system shall record every identity-proofing event and every credential issued.
statement: NFR-EPCS-010: The system shall retain a record of every identity proofing and every credential issued.

gold_statement: The system shall require each grant or revocation of signing access to be entered by one designated individual.
statement: The system shall enforce logical access control over the signing function using two individuals.

gold_statement: The system shall display the DEA attestation statement with the prescription details while prompting for two-factor authentication.
statement: The system shall prompt the prescriber to authenticate using two-factor authentication before signing a controlled prescription.

gold_statement: The system shall allow a prescriber to sign with a password and a hard token without using a biometric factor.
statement: FR-EPCS-021: The system shall implement two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token at the signing step, as stated in S-PRES-40.

gold_statement: The system shall revoke a practitioner's signing access on the same day a lost token or lapsed registration is reported.
statement: The system shall maintain an internal audit trail with daily analysis and incident reporting for controlled substances prescriptions, including revocation of signing access on the same day we learn a token is lost or a registration has lapsed.

gold_statement: The system shall allow only the practitioner whose DEA registration number appears on a prescription to sign it.
statement: The system shall not allow alteration of the prescription information after it has been digitally signed.

gold_statement: The system shall allow a manually signed replacement to be printed only after a failed-transmission notice, stating the pharmacy and the date and time of the failed transmission.
statement: The system shall allow printing of a prescription after transmission only if it is clearly labeled as a copy not for dispensing.

gold_statement: The system shall complete the signing step, including two-factor authentication, within 20 seconds for 95% of signings.
statement: NFR-EPCS-044: The system shall implement two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token at the signing function.

gold_statement: The application shall be re-audited whenever signing functionality changes or every two years, whichever comes first.
statement: The system shall not be used for controlled substances until the third-party audit has passed, and it must undergo re-audits whenever signing functionality changes or every two years as stated in S-COMP-17.

gold_statement: The organisation shall report security incidents affecting prescription records to the DEA within one business day.
statement: The system shall keep records as the DEA requires.

gold_statement: The system shall issue credential activation information through two separate channels.
statement: The system shall provide identity proofing and credential issuance for practitioners.
